structure:
One short ruling file, workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-sam-2026-11-09.md, 30 lines in four pieces. A title line naming Sam and 9 November 2026; a one-line preamble saying design questions 13 and 10 were decided by Sam after the waiting-on-design evidence review of the same day; the ruling quoted verbatim as two blockquotes ("Yea I agree drop it." and the three-line shout on address search, which calls templates and address search concept work mixed into "get this done" work and says address search is not something to build yet); then an unquoted paragraph of the main session's own context on the review recommendation, the row's three screen-reader criteria, the prototype's hand-built country search and main's GOV.UK accessible autocomplete. Last, a '## Decided' section of three numbered claims the main session read from the quotes: (1) the country search keeps the accessible autocomplete's own announcements, dropping the 'Country search results' label and 'Selected <country>' announcement on live animals, germinal products and high-risk plants origin pages, with inc-189 dropped and req-020 out of scope; (2) address search is concept work and parked, add-address pages keep every field shown from the start as main has them, inc-194 deferred and its requirements adopted but parked; (3) Design Release 2.1 mixes concept work with deadline work, so a row is checked for deadline need before it goes to the designer or the build loop and flagged to Sam rather than built, a feature main lacks entirely being the usual sign. The scope is the whole file, so nothing is left out. The file has no tables, images or links, and the two blockquotes are the only words of the owner: the context paragraph and the three numbered items are the main session's reading and must be checked against those quotes.

Extracted in 1 part:
Part 1, The whole ruling file: Part 1 read the whole of workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-sam-2026-11-09.md, every line from the title to the end of decided item 3, and claims all of it. The file has four pieces: a title line naming Sam and 9 November 2026; a one-line preamble saying design questions 13 and 10 were decided by Sam after the waiting-on-design evidence review of the same day; the owner's words quoted verbatim as two blockquotes (the one-line 'Yea I agree drop it.' and a three-line shout on address search that calls it not a deadline job, names templates as concept work mixed into the 'get this done work', and says address search is not something to build yet); an unquoted context paragraph of the main session's own reading (the review recommendation, the row's three screen-reader criteria including Welsh versions, the prototype's hand-built country search with no label, dead arrow keys and the typed country lost without JavaScript, and main's GOV.UK accessible autocomplete announcing result count, highlighted option and chosen value); and a '## Decided' section of three numbered items. The claims cover decided item 1 (the country search keeps the accessible autocomplete's own announcements, no 'Country search results' label and no 'Selected <country>' announcement on the live animals, germinal products and high-risk plants origin pages, inc-189 dropped, req-020 out of scope, design question 13 off the designer's list), decided item 2 (address search concept work and parked, not built for the deadline, add-address pages keep every field shown from the start as main has them, inc-194 deferred with its requirements adopted but parked, design question 10 not going to the designer now) and decided item 3 (the standing rule that Design Release 2.1 mixes concept work with deadline work, so a row is checked for deadline need before it goes to the designer or the build loop, a feature main lacks entirely being the usual sign, and such a row flagged to Sam rather than built). Only the two blockquotes are the owner's words, so claims resting on them alone are verbatim and everything the decided items add beyond them (the page list, the inc/req dispositions, the add-address field behaviour, the ask-first rule and the main-lacks-it test) is inferred with the statement saying what in the quote implies it. Nothing in the context paragraph is recorded as a decision. Three gaps record what the file touches and leaves open: the Welsh versions of the dropped announcements, what becomes of the templates work beyond being called concept work, and who unparks address search and when. The file has no tables, images or links, and nothing in it belongs to another part.

claims.statement: The owner agrees to drop the change that was proposed to what a screen reader hears on the country search, so nothing is built for it.
claims.quote: Yea I agree drop it.
claims.note: Answers design question 13, decided after the waiting-on-design evidence review of 9 November 2026 that the file's preamble names. The surrounding context paragraph says this agreed with the review's recommendation, but that sentence is the main session's own words, not the owner's.

claims.statement: Address search is not to be built yet.
claims.quote: but yea the address earch aint something we need to build yet
claims.note: Answers design question 10. The quote's 'earch' is the owner's own spelling, left as written.

claims.statement: Address search is not work that has to be done for the deadline.
claims.quote: The shout on address search is it's not a "get done for our deadline job"
claims.note: Answers design question 10, alongside claim ruling-sam-2026-11-09-p1-002.

claims.statement: Templates in Design Release 2.1 are concept work.
claims.quote: some of the stuff in dr 2.1 (like templates) is concept work

claims.statement: Design Release 2.1 mixes concept work in with the work that has to be done for the deadline, and that mixing is confusing.
claims.quote: which is mixed in with the "get this done work" making things confusing

claims.statement: Address search is itself concept work: the quote puts address search on the not-for-the-deadline side of the same concept-work-versus-deadline-work split it draws for templates, so it follows that address search is concept work rather than deadline work.
claims.ref: ruling-sam-2026-11-09.md claim 2, read against the second blockquote
claims.quote: The shout on address search is it's not a "get done for our deadline job" some of the stuff in dr 2.1 (like templates) is concept work, which is mixed in with the "get this done work" making things confusing. but yea the address earch aint something we need to build yet
claims.note: Decided item 2's heading calls it concept work in so many words; the owner's own words name only templates as concept work, so this is recorded as inferred.

claims.statement: The country search's screen-reader announcements stay as the accessible autocomplete already makes them, with nothing added on top: the owner's agreement to drop the proposed change leaves the component's own announcements as the behaviour.
claims.quote: **The country search keeps the accessible autocomplete's own announcements.** Design question 13.
claims.note: Rests on the owner's 'Yea I agree drop it.'; the naming of the accessible autocomplete is the main session's reading, so this is inferred, not verbatim.

claims.statement: No 'Country search results' list label is built for the country search.
claims.quote: No 'Country search results' label and no 'Selected <country>' announcement, on the live animals, germinal products or high-risk plants origin pages.
claims.note: The owner's words are only 'Yea I agree drop it.'; the label is one of the dropped row's criteria as the main session's context paragraph names them, so dropping it follows from the quote but is not in the owner's words.

claims.statement: No 'Selected <country>' announcement is built for the country search.
claims.quote: No 'Country search results' label and no 'Selected <country>' announcement, on the live animals, germinal products or high-risk plants origin pages.
claims.note: As with claim ruling-sam-2026-11-09-p1-008, this follows from 'Yea I agree drop it.' applying to the row whose criteria the context paragraph lists, rather than from the owner's own words.

claims.statement: The drop of the two announcements applies on the live animals origin page, the germinal products origin page and the high-risk plants origin page.
claims.quote: on the live animals, germinal products or high-risk plants origin pages
claims.note: The page list is the main session's reading of where the dropped row applied; the owner's words name no page.

claims.statement: Increment inc-189 is dropped.
claims.quote: inc-189 is dropped and req-020 is out of scope.
claims.note: The backlog disposition is the main session's reading of 'Yea I agree drop it.'; the owner names no increment.

claims.statement: Requirement req-020 is out of scope.
claims.quote: inc-189 is dropped and req-020 is out of scope.
claims.note: As with claim ruling-sam-2026-11-09-p1-011, the requirement disposition follows from the agreed drop but is not in the owner's words.

claims.statement: Design question 13 no longer goes to the designer.
claims.quote: The question no longer goes to the designer.
claims.note: Follows from the owner settling the question with 'Yea I agree drop it.'; the owner does not say it himself.

claims.statement: The add-address pages show every field from the start, as the real service's main branch has them, rather than offering an address search first.
claims.quote: The add-address pages keep every field shown from the start, as main has them.
claims.note: Follows from address search not being built yet; the owner says nothing about the add-address pages' fields.

claims.statement: Increment inc-194 is deferred.
claims.quote: inc-194 is deferred and its requirements stay adopted but parked, so the question does not go to the designer now.
claims.note: The increment disposition is the main session's reading of 'the address earch aint something we need to build yet'.

claims.statement: The requirements behind the address-search increment stay adopted but parked rather than being dropped.
claims.quote: inc-194 is deferred and its requirements stay adopted but parked, so the question does not go to the designer now.
claims.note: Follows from 'aint something we need to build yet' — not yet, rather than never; the owner does not use the words adopted or parked.

claims.statement: Design question 10 does not go to the designer now.
claims.quote: so the question does not go to the designer now
claims.note: Follows from the owner parking the work; the owner does not mention the designer.

claims.statement: Before a Design Release 2.1 row goes to the designer or into the build loop, someone asks whether it is needed for the deadline.
claims.quote: Before a Design Release 2.1 row goes to the designer or the build loop, ask whether it is needed for the deadline;
claims.note: A standing rule the main session draws from the owner's complaint that concept work is 'mixed in with the "get this done work" making things confusing'; the owner states the problem, not this rule.

claims.statement: A feature the real service's main branch does not have at all, shown only in the prototype, is the usual sign that a row is concept work.
claims.quote: a feature main does not have at all, shown only in the prototype, is the usual sign of concept work
claims.note: The test for spotting concept work is the main session's reading; the owner gives templates and address search as instances but no test.

claims.statement: A row judged to be concept work is flagged to Sam rather than built.
claims.quote: Flag it to Sam rather than build it.
claims.note: Follows from the owner being the one who ruled on templates and address search; the owner does not ask to be flagged.

claims.statement: The ruling leaves open whether the Welsh versions of the 'Country search results' label and the 'Selected <country>' announcement are also dropped: the context paragraph counts them as one of the dropped row's three criteria, but neither the owner's words nor decided item 1 mentions Welsh.
claims.ref: ruling-sam-2026-11-09.md, context paragraph (lines 11 to 12) against claim 1

claims.statement: The ruling leaves open what happens to the templates work: it calls templates concept work but does not say whether templates are parked, deferred, dropped or still built for the deadline, and names no increment or requirement for them.
The ruling leaves open who picks the parked address-search work back up, when, and what would unpark it: it says only that it is not needed yet.
